sentences.text: Ankit Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025

Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:2565
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 7 th Of February, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 527 of 2025
 Ankit Sahu
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pallav Tripathi - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Rohit Mishra -Public Prosecutor for the responde
 Shri Shiv Pratap Singh Kushwah - Advocate for the res
 Order

1. This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed against the order dated 06.01.2025 passed by Special Judge (SC/ST (P.A.) Act, District Shivpuri(M.P) in Bail Application 1209/2024 whereby the application moved by the appellant for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been rejected in connection with Crime No.469/2024 registered at Police Station Pichhore, District Shivpuri for the offences punishable under Sections 376 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3(1)(w)(i) &
3(2)(v) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: 2. The allegation against the present appellant is of committing rape with the prosecutrix on the pretext of solemnizing marriage with her.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:2565 2 CRA-527-2025 3.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the present appellant that appellant is in custody since 12.12.2024.
Charge-sheet has been filed on 30.01.2025.

As per the story of prosecution, the applicant has committed rape with the prosecutrix on the pretext of solemnizing marriage with her but the FSL report is negative and, therefore, the DNA examination was not conducted.
It is also submitted that the present applicant is innocent and has been falsely implication in this case.
There is no criminal antecedent against the present appellant.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the appellant.

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as the learned counsel for the complainant opposed the bail application and pray for its rejection.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this appeal is allowed by setting aside the order dated 06.01.2025 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST (P.A) Act, Shivpuri in Bail Application No.1209/2024 and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
In case, if he is found involving in the offence of the same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.

v) The appellant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and vi) The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
8. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
C.C. per rules.
